ns0:entry.ns0:content:
chore(mypy): cover processor (#4757)

Enable the lerobot.processor.* mypy override and fix the 65 errors it surfaced under the CI gate.
- isinstance(x, PolicyAction/EnvAction) -> concrete torch.Tensor/np.ndarray (the aliases collapse to Any without stubs); annotations keep the aliases. GripperPenaltyProcessorStep only rejects dict actions, so every input it accepted before still passes.
- Tuple literals for the TransitionKey groups in DeviceProcessorStep so the Literal key union survives; Optional info/complementary_data are narrowed with `if x is None: x = {}`, which keeps the caller's dict identity; create_transition params widened to match EnvTransition.
- ValueError guards (the module convention) in make_default_policy_processor_steps and the relative/gripper action steps; all seven DataProcessorPipeline.process_* methods share _require_component, so a step that nulls the requested component raises instead of returning None under a non-Optional return type.
- Typed ProcessorStepRegistry (dict[str, type[ProcessorStep]], generic register, _registry_name: ClassVar[str]); the HasTeleopEvents protocol replaces the misused TeleopWithEvents TypeVar, which is removed (no users in src/tests/docs/examples); a private _TeleopInfo alias bridges the Enum-keyed HIL info dict with two casts.
- Two new type: ignores: [override] on RenderTrainingMessagesStep.__call__ (returns None to drop a sample) and [index] on a latent LiberoProcessorStep key bug kept for behaviour parity. Two stale [assignment] ignores in normalize_processor.py dropped (--warn-unused-ignores), and DeviceProcessorStep.__post_init__ annotated so the gate checks its body.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: chore(mypy): cover robot (#4754)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
chore(mypy): cover robot (#4754)

* chore(mypy): cover lerobot_types

Replace `TransitionKey(str, Enum)` with a `@final` constants class whose members
are `Final[Literal[...]]` strings, and rewrite `EnvTransition` as a class-based
`TypedDict` with the seven literal keys (all required). mypy cannot index a
TypedDict with a str-Enum member (it reports the member NAME as a missing key)
and rejects non-literal field names in the functional `TypedDict(...)` form, so
the old definitions left `EnvTransition` with no usable fields for every module
that handles transitions. With the new spelling `td[TransitionKey.X]`,
`.get(...)`, `.copy()` and dict literals keyed by `TransitionKey.X` type-check
with no call-site changes. The explicit `Final[Literal["x"]]` form (rather than
the implicit `Final = "x"`) keeps the literal type when a member is bound to a
local or a tuple variable; only a `list` of members widens to `list[str]`.
`PolicyAction` and `EnvAction` get an explicit `TypeAlias` because their
torch/numpy targets resolve to `Any` under the CI mypy config
(`follow_imports = skip`, no stubs); a PEP 695 `type` statement is not usable
since both are `isinstance` targets.

Enable the `lerobot.lerobot_types` mypy override in pyproject.toml and drop the
Enum-only `.value` accesses and the `isinstance(k, TransitionKey)` assertion in
tests: tests/processor/{test_act,test_diffusion,test_gaussian_actor,
test_smolvla,test_tdmpc,test_vqbet}_processor.py, tests/processor/test_pipeline.py,
tests/rewards/test_classifier_processor.py, tests/test_interactive_rollout.py.

BREAKING (intentional, no compat shim): `TransitionKey` is no longer an `Enum`.
`TransitionKey("observation")`, `TransitionKey["OBSERVATION"]`,
`list(TransitionKey)`, `"observation" in TransitionKey`, `.value` / `.name` and
`__members__` now raise; `isinstance(x, TransitionKey)` is always False; `str()`
/ f-strings render `"observation"` instead of `"TransitionKey.OBSERVATION"`.
Nothing in src/, tests/, examples/ or docs/ used these. Consequences:
- Pickles of transitions written by older versions fail to load with
  `TypeError: TransitionKey() takes no arguments` (Enum reduce calls the class);
  no in-repo cross-version path exists. `torch.load(weights_only=True)` of a
  transition, which failed on Enum keys, now works.
- `ValueError("Cannot filter batched field ...")` in
  processor/render_messages_processor.py now names `'observation.foo'` /
  `'action'` instead of `'TransitionKey.OBSERVATION.foo'`; no test pins the text.
- `EnvTransition.__annotations__` holds lazy strings (the module already uses
  `from __future__ import annotations`); use `typing.get_type_hints`.

Left for the not-yet-gated modules' own PRs: rewards/{topreward,robometer}/
compute_rabc_weights.py and policies/lawam/processor_lawam.py pass partial dict
literals where an `EnvTransition` is expected (mypy: Missing keys), and
processor/device_processor.py iterates *lists* of keys, which widen to `str`.

* chore(mypy): cover robots

Enable the lerobot.robots.* mypy override (54 CI-gate errors -> 0).

Optional connection state (zmq context/sockets, threads, the B601 motor bus) is now
annotated at declaration and narrowed with DeviceNotConnectedError guards; calibration
ticks are coerced to int for MotorCalibration; the kinematic processor copies the total
EnvTransition TypedDict as one and keeps tolerant .get() reads of complementary_data;
robot locals/attributes use the shared RobotObservation/RobotAction/Camera types. New
DepthCamera runtime-checkable Protocol in lerobot.cameras replaces getattr(cam, "use_depth")
duck typing at the eight depth-read sites and in so_follower._cameras_ft, so observation
features and get_observation() share one predicate (regression test added). lekiwi_client
uses the module-top _zmq_available/require_package guard. One type: ignore[import-untyped]
(requests stubs absent from the pre-commit env).

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
chore(mypy): cover jobs (#4753)

Enable the mypy override for lerobot.jobs.* (ignore_errors = false) and fix the

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
chore(mypy): cover utils (#4735)

Enable the lerobot.utils.* mypy override (ignore_errors = false); the CI gate
went from 31 errors in 9 files to 0.

- import_utils: @overload is_package_available so the _foo_available flags type as bool
  (tuple[bool, str] with a keyword return_version=True, the union for a runtime bool);
  order-preserving dedup via dict.fromkeys.
- utils: sys.platform == "win32" narrowing for the Windows-only msvcrt / CREATE_NO_WINDOW
  paths; flatten_dict/unflatten_dict typed dict[str, Any]; enter_pressed returns a real bool.
- transition: move_transition_to_device binds torch.device to a new local and indexes the
  TypedDict with the literal "action" key so the file type-checks on its own under the
  pre-commit hook (pass_filenames + follow_imports=skip); Transition.reward/done/truncated
  widened to `| torch.Tensor`, matching the body's isinstance branches and EnvTransition.
- feature_utils: hw_to_dataset_features takes Mapping[str, type | tuple[int, ...] | PolicyFeature]
  (pipeline_features passes PolicyFeature values; Mapping because dict is invariant) and
  returns dict[str, dict[str, Any]].
- process / keyboard_input: multiprocessing.synchronize.Event imported at module level (stdlib,
  as in transport/utils.py); TYPE_CHECKING-guarded pynput import replaces the conflicting
  runtime re-import; precise locals (collate, feature_utils); `-> None` on touched signatures.
- random_utils: isinstance narrowing on numpy's dict | tuple RNG state (local mypy: 0 residual).
- 8 type: ignore[attr-defined] for function-attribute live-stream state in foxglove/rerun; 0 casts.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs (#4732)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs (#4732)

A tag is mutable: whoever controls the action's repository can move
`v4` to different code, and the next run picks it up with no diff to
review. Pinning to the commit SHA freezes the code that runs today.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: perf(unitree_g1): cap ONNX Runtime thread pool for the G1 controllers…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
perf(unitree_g1): cap ONNX Runtime thread pool for the G1 controllers (#4264)

Add make_ort_session_options() to g1_utils and use it in every controller that
opens an ONNX session: GR00T (balance + walk), Holosoma, and the SONIC decoder.
These are small MLPs stepped at 50 Hz from a background thread alongside the torch
upper-body/VLA policy and IK; by default ORT spins up a thread per core, which
starves the real-time control loop and makes rollouts stutter. Cap the pool to
1 intra / 1 inter thread -- lowest-latency for per-step inference -- and quiet
ORT logging.

Co-authored-by: Steven Palma <imstevenpmwork@ieee.org>
